GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale: The format work continues a 2026-08-21 session (commit 8f52f0c) that fixed plan tasks and waves to element-name identity (TASK-T-NNN, WAVE-N) after auditing the package against the user's own prompting guide (~/dev/global-docs/prompt-engineering-best-practices-v3.md, section 10: stable types versus unique identities, unique closing boundaries). That audit deliberately left spec components, plan architecture modules, and the whole design-context template unfixed. The trigger for finishing was a Telegram chat critique of "greppable XML" (grep has no XML semantics, child id tags were called a sign of a badly chosen format, XPath was suggested), which formally matched the guide's own rules, plus the user noticing the remaining violations. Components and modules now share one identity space: the plan architecture section is the spec's component map continued into the next document, so the same COMPONENT-UPPER-SLUG appears in both and the plan-components-subset-of-spec-components check becomes mechanical. The user stated flatly that a plan module without a spec component does not exist, which turned traceability into a hard invariant rather than a convention.

The linter exists because of an asymmetry established during the 2026-08-21 session: grep won over xmllint for model-facing helpers because grep is present in effectively all training corpora including small executor models (9b/27b), while xmllint is absent from tool whitelists and small models fail on unfamiliar tool chains (Codex CLI auto-approve whitelist lacks xmllint; BFCL scores collapse below ~7B on multi-step tool chains; OpenAI wires rg into the root prompt because even popular tools do not surface on their own). The correct conclusion is not "no validation" but "validation is not the model's job": models keep grep/sed as the query layer, and the host enforces invariants deterministically. This moves format enforcement from model discipline to code, which works identically on a 9b executor and an xhigh planner.

The parser choice reversed during design. An initial lean toward a hand-written mini-parser (motivated by dependency conservatism and the tiny attribute-free dialect) was challenged by the user. Honest re-analysis: hand-rolling entity handling, CDATA edge cases, and error positions is exactly where silent parser bugs live, and a linter that mis-parses is worse than none. The decisive fact is that htmlparser2 (^12.0.0) is already a runtime dependency used by web-tools, has a real xmlMode, and emits tag, attribute, CDATA, and comment events with token positions. The in-repo part therefore shrinks to a strict stack validator (balance, single root, stray content) on top of a battle-tested tokenizer, which is small and fully testable. The strictness gap (htmlparser2 is lenient by HTML heritage and will not itself reject unclosed tags) is acceptable because the stack validator owns that job by design.

The plugin posture follows the peak-hours lesson: a hard block in the wrong hook destroyed user messages until it moved to chat.params, and validation of a write is only meaningful after the write happens. Writes are therefore validated in tool.execute.after, warn mode only appends verdict text, and enforce fails a tool call solely on ERROR-severity findings. Severity is lifecycle-aware by construction: draft documents are legitimately incomplete mid-interview, so structural emptiness is never an ERROR at draft status and becomes one only at approved/applied, while format, identity, and reference rules stay strict at every status. This is the user's non-negotiable constraint: in-progress composition and editing must never be blocked.

The cache is content-addressed rather than mtime-based because same-size edits and preserved mtimes would produce stale verdicts silently. Keys combine every input content hash (a plan verdict keys on the plan bytes plus the referenced spec bytes, because cross-file invariants make the spec an input of the plan verdict) with a lintVersion constant bumped whenever the rule set changes. Files are tens of kilobytes, so the cache is not a performance rescue; it exists so the read hook costs effectively nothing on every read, verdicts are stable objects instead of flickering recomputations, and cold CLI starts reuse cross-session results. A --no-cache flag exists for debugging, and no enforce-specific freshness rule is needed: content-addressed results are correct by construction when keys are complete, and a just-written file always misses.

Vocabulary unification settled on snake_case for field names because plan and design-context templates already use it, fields rhyme with the code identifiers tasks reference, and it collapses three coexisting conventions (kebab-case spec fields, snake_case plan fields, CAPS identity slugs) into one writable rule: fields are snake_case semantic types, addressable entities are UPPER-SLUG element names, attributes are forbidden, code is CDATA-wrapped. The plan's design-context path element becomes design_context for uniformity even though the file name stays design-context.xml, because element names and file names are different layers. GRACE PascalCase documents are a separate system owned by grace-cli and are intentionally untouched.

Archive exclusion is a policy decision, not a limitation: archived packages are immutable historical evidence under repository policy, they predate the new format so they would fail rules they were never written under, and read annotation on archived files would add noise to legitimate historical lookups. An --archive flag still allows explicit audit runs, for example when reviewing how far old formats drifted.

Execution note: T-004 also had to touch src/commands/plugin-toggle.test.ts because its canonical toggle-list count assertion is content-coupled to PLUGIN_TOGGLE_NAMES; the file was missed during planning scope enumeration and was added to ObservedWriteScope during execution rather than through a supersede cycle. No other planning assumption changed.

Alternatives.Alternative: Attribute-based identity (task/component id attributes) was rejected: artifacts stay attribute-free by standing decision, and closing boundaries would remain generic.
Comment-style repeated boundaries (END SLUG comments) was rejected as inconsistent with the already-shipped TASK-T-NNN element-name decision.

A separate MODULE- prefix for plan architecture was rejected in favor of one shared COMPONENT- space, because plan modules are spec components continued, and the user confirmed plan-only modules do not exist.
fast-xml-parser as a new dependency (XMLValidator with line and column out of the box) was rejected because htmlparser2 already in the tree covers the need with zero new supply chain.
A from-scratch XML parser was rejected after the user challenged it: entity, CDATA, and position edge cases are silent-bug territory and already solved by the existing tokenizer dependency.
xmllint or XPath in any layer was rejected: not in model training priors, hard-failing, and unnecessary once the format itself carries identity.
mtime-plus-size cache keys were rejected in favor of content hashes because stale-verdict correctness dominates and hashing is effectively free at these file sizes.
Enforce-by-default plugin mode was rejected: warn is safe by construction (append-only verdicts), and blocking is an explicit user opt-in per the peak-hours soft-default lesson.
Read-time archive heuristics (warning when reading archived packages) were rejected to keep the plugin dumb and deterministic; archive policy stays in the lint command's skip note.
Auto-fix mode was rejected because spec content is semantic; suggesting machine repairs to requirements documents invites quiet meaning drift.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: The exact warning-severity rule set (which non-ERROR findings exist beyond layout notes) is pinned during planning with the first fixture corpus.
The JSON output schema field names for verdict objects are finalized during implementation together with the command tests.
Whether vvoc lint grows a package.json script or CI wiring for downstream repositories that commit .vvoc/specs is a follow-up; this repository gitignores .vvoc so CI here is not applicable.
Lint coverage for .vvoc/lessons and .vvoc/runbooks is a possible follow-up change with its own format contract; out of scope here.

A future eval per prompting-guide section 15.2 comparing generic versus identity markup on working models remains open; the identity benefit is an architecture-derived inference, not a proven universal.

Scenarios.Scenario: An agent composes a spec section by section during a vv-spec interview in enforce mode: every intermediate save is a valid draft with empty fields, writes succeed throughout, and only a malformed reference or an attribute would fail a save.

An agent reads plan.xml mid-execution after a teammate hand-edited it and broke a component slug: the read output ends with the lint verdict listing the ERROR with file and line, before the agent trusts the file.

A plan renames a component slug locally but the spec still has the old one: vvoc lint and the plugin both report plan architecture component absent from spec, making the traceability break loud instead of silent.
A spec.xml edit lands between two lint runs: the next plan lint recomputes because the spec hash inside the plan cache key changed, while unrelated packages still hit the cache.
A user audits migration drift by running vvoc lint --archive over the specs tree: archived packages are included explicitly, while the default run still skips them with a visible count.
A downstream repository commits .vvoc/specs and runs vvoc lint --strict --format json in CI: exit code one on any warning, verdict objects parsed by the pipeline.
